modules.name: Datum and CRS registry
modules.design_question: Which horizontal frame and vertical datum let City LiDAR, HRDEM/MRDEM, LidarBC, SRTM, footprints and cone geodetic heights agree to centimetres, with realisation and epoch recorded for every layer?
modules.method: Canonical frame: EPSG:3157 (NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N) and CGVD28 as realised in City LiDAR (CGVD28GVRD, geoid HTMVBC00, epoch 1997; GeoBC calls HTMVBC00 equivalent to HTGVRDBC00, which LTSA 465C approves in Metro Vancouver). Tag every layer with horizontal realisation, epoch, vertical datum, geoid file and source edition. Convert CGVD2013a layers (HRDEM, MRDEM, LidarBC 2025) to CGVD28 by inverting PROJ grid ca_nrc_HT2_1997_CGG2013a.tif (1997 epoch, like HTMVBC00); compare the HT2_2010v70 variant (EPSG:10520). Measure the residual with a same-source pair: City DEM 2013 (CGVD28) against HRDEM VILLE_VANCOUVER 2013 (CGVD2013, assumed built from the same points); fix the vgridshift sign in a unit test on that pair, then confirm on City 2022 flat open ground. Convert EGM96 (SRTM) and EGM2008 (GLO-30) through PROJ grids. Transform layers labelled EPSG:26910 with explicit NTv2 operation EPSG:9119 (BC_93_05), assert the transformer is not ballpark, and test on LiDAR roof corners. Render each view in a local ENU frame (grid scale 0.9996, curvature). Treat Vista as a distorted legacy frame (C02-M07). Confirm the cone datum with views@vancouver.ca before any compliance wording.
inputs: PROJ grids: HT2_1997, HT2_2010v70, BC_93_05, EGM96, EGM2008
Public Views Guidelines s.2 'maximum geodetic height'

parameters.name: Z_CGVD2013a vs Z_CGVD28
parameters.relationship: Z_2013 = Z_28 + grid(x,y), grid = HT2 hybrid geoid minus CGG2013a (EPSG remarks). Epoch variants 1997, 2002, 2010 list accuracy 0.0, 0.02, 0.03 m. CHS offsets imply about +0.12 m at Vancouver. PROJ sign (multiplier -1) unverified.

parameters.name: Geoid and epoch per layer
parameters.relationship: City 2022: CGVD28GVRD with HTMVBC00 (HTGVRDBC00 extended east). LTSA approves HTGVRDBC00 in Metro Vancouver and HTv2.0 (1997.0) elsewhere. National grids exist for epochs 1997, 2002, 2010; the local effect of epoch is unquantified.

parameters.name: Ellipsoidal vs orthometric
parameters.relationship: h_ellipsoidal = H_orthometric + N; N differs by model (CGG2013a, HTMVBC00, EGM96, EGM2008), so heights from different models must not be mixed.

parameters.name: UTM grid scale k
parameters.relationship: k = 0.999601 at the Vista anchor (E 491.2 km, computed); ground distance = grid distance / k, a 0.4 m/km shortening (12 m at 30 km).

parameters.name: Earth-curvature drop
parameters.relationship: drop = d^2/(2R) x (1 - k_ref); 70.6 m at 30 km, 61.5 m with refraction k_ref 0.13. Hand calculation.

parameters.name: MRDEM edition shift
parameters.relationship: v1.1 changed the datum transformation (about 40 cm average change); v1.2 fixed a 1 to 3 pixel offset where HRDEM is the source. GLO-30 was converted with CGG2013. Pin and record the edition.

parameters.name: NAD83 to NAD83(CSRS) in BC
parameters.relationship: EPSG:9119 NAD83 to NAD83(CSRS)v4 uses NTv2 BC_93_05 (accuracy 0.1, unit unstated). City orthophotos are labelled EPSG:26910; whether the pixels are truly original NAD83 is unverified (test on roof corners).

modules.name: Footprint authority and conflation
modules.design_question: Which polygon represents each downtown building today, including post-2015 towers, with podium and tower parts separated and parcel-split polygons not mistaken for change?
modules.method: 1) Reproject City 2015 footprints (154,124 polygons) to EPSG:3157. 2) Build a LiDAR building mask from City 2022 building-class returns more than 2.5 m above ground, 0.5 m raster. 3) Split mask components where adjacent roof heights differ by more than 3 m, so podiums and towers separate. 4) Match by one-sided coverage, not IoU: c_poly (share of the polygon inside the mask) and c_part (share of the mask part assigned to that polygon by nearest-polygon partition); use IoU only for free-standing buildings. Mask-only parts are new, polygon-only are demolished, middling values are changed. 5) Outline source: buildings with roof 30 m or more above ground take regularised LiDAR outlines (simplify 0.25 to 0.5 m, snap within 5 degrees), because 2015 orthophoto tracing can carry relief displacement; lower buildings keep City polygons. 6) Dissolve parcel-split polygons inside one mask part when roof P90 differs under 1 m. 7) OSM only as a separate optional overlay; Overture and City 2009 as cross-checks. 8) Give every feature id, fp_source, fp_year, lidar_date, change flag. 9) QA on LiDAR DSM hillshade; hand-check the 100 tallest towers; test everything on tile 490000_5459000 first.

modules.name: LiDAR LOD1 height extraction
modules.design_question: How are robust roof and base heights derived per footprint from 49 points per square metre LiDAR, including rooftop appurtenances and towers finished after the survey?
modules.method: Per footprint, use City 2022 points inside the polygon shrunk 0.5 m. Assign points to footprints through a 0.25 m polygon-id raster (array lookup, not per-point geometry tests). Keep building-class first returns; drop spikes (z more than 5 MAD from the 1 m cell median). Compute P50, P75, P90, P95, P99 and max directly from the point population, the operator behind the 3D BAG benchmark; if PDAL rasters are used instead, label the result 'P90 of 0.5 m cell maxima' and compare both on the synthetic roof. Ground = P10 of ground-class points in a 0.5 to 2 m ring, else the DTM. Store absolute roof elevation in the canonical datum and height above ground, with n_roof, n_ground, flat-roof flag. Post-2022 towers: difference the City 2022 surface against LidarBC 2025 points (8 pts/m2, CGVD2013, classes 1, 2, 7, 12, no building class) and set built_after_lidar. Core scope: P90 and max only; defer podium/tower part clustering (LoD1.3) and per-percentile RMSE to v1. For cone tests use max and list minor rooftop items for review (clause 3.1.2; appurtenances count under 3.1.1); display P90. Cross-check against published heights.
outputs: per-building roof percentiles, ground, quality fields, built_after_lidar flag

modules.name: Downtown ground surface and cone-height interface
modules.design_question: What is bare-earth elevation Z_ground(x,y) in the cone datum, and how are cone limits published as absolute geodetic elevation first and above-ground estimates second, without implying a zoning height?
modules.method: Tile rule: 1 km tiles (named by SW corner UTM) intersecting a 1.5 km circle (13 tiles, ring R0) or a 2 km circle (20 tiles) around E 491221.8, N 5458890.0. Scripted GET to webtransfer.vancouver.ca returns 403 for a default client, so download in a browser, record size and sha256, process one tile at a time (laspy chunks or PDAL) in a scratch folder outside the repo, then delete the LAS. Ground-class points give a 1 m DTM and a DSM; TIN-fill under buildings and water. Check against 2018 and 2013 LiDAR. Convert to the canonical datum (M01). Publish a 2 m DTM or error-bounded mesh. Primary output: each cone's maximum geodetic elevation in the canonical datum. Secondary: h_allow = H_cone minus Z_ground, labelled 'above 2022 bare earth, not the bylaw base surface'. View origin Z = DTM at origin plus eye height (default 1.68 m, unverified). Carry sigma_allow beside every value and mark every figure 'estimate' until the City confirms the datum. Add a regression: existing towers that predate cone amendments must sit at or below the reconstructed H_cone or be listed exceptions.
outputs: Z_ground(x,y) and cone-elevation interface with sigma

parameters.name: Allowed height above ground
parameters.relationship: h_allow(x,y) = H_cone minus Z_ground(x,y), both in one vertical datum; a ground error moves the limit one-for-one.

parameters.name: Error budget
parameters.relationship: sigma_allow = sqrt(sigma_cone^2 + sigma_ground^2 + sigma_datum^2); LiDAR 0.081 m (95%) is about 0.04 m at 1 sigma if Gaussian.

parameters.name: SRTM propagation
parameters.relationship: Delta h_allow = minus Delta Z_ground; SRTM actual vertical error about 10 m (16 m LE90 specification) gives a limit error of the same size.

parameters.name: Interpolation error
parameters.relationship: Linear interpolation error bound is (cell^2/8) x max second derivative; dense LiDAR keeps flat downtown error far below sensor noise.

parameters.name: Bylaw base surface vs LiDAR ground
parameters.relationship: Bylaw height is measured from a base surface built from official building grades at site corners (By-law 13067, search summary, unopened). LiDAR bare earth differs by an unquantified amount; never present h_allow as a zoning height.

parameters.name: View origin eye height
parameters.relationship: Origin Z = Z_ground + 1.68 m (average 5 ft 6 in viewer per a 2023 City memo, search summary only); unverified parameter.

modules.name: Multi-resolution terrain and North Shore backdrop
modules.design_question: How should terrain be tiered from 1 m downtown to 30 m mountains 10 to 50 km away, given that open 1 m LiDAR does not reach the North Shore peaks?
modules.method: Measure coverage first. NRCan HRDEM extent polygons, HRDEM mosaic point queries and the LidarBC point-cloud tile index agree: 1 m LiDAR reaches the lower slopes to about 49.38 N, a valley strip east of Grouse (2016) and a western strip (2019), but not the Grouse or Seymour summit samples or the Lions. Rings: R0 0 to 1.5 km, City DTM 1 m. R1 1.5 to 6 km: City LiDAR to its 49.32 N limit, then LidarBC or HRDEM 1 m where a tile exists, resampled to 2 to 5 m. R2 6 to 25 km: 1 m LiDAR resampled to 10 m where covered, else MRDEM-30 at native 30 m (do not upsample). R3 25 to 50 km: MRDEM-30. Use DTM for ground and DSM for skylines; keep canopy separate. Convert every ring via M01 and calibrate offsets on overlaps. Mesh with Delatin or RTIN under error epsilon(d) = tau x d x HFOV/width; share boundary vertices or add skirts; apply curvature at render time. Check skylines against peak maxima found by local search, not a single sample. Request ridge LiDAR from LidarBC, Metro Vancouver and the North and West Vancouver districts.

modules.name: Compact storage and web delivery
modules.design_question: Which formats and tiling keep every layer inside GitHub Pages limits yet load quickly in the browser?
modules.method: Store buildings as quantised footprint rings plus attributes (id, base elevation, roof percentiles, flags) and triangulate in the browser with earcut. Store terrain as per-ring quantised int16 height tiles or meshes with deflate or zstd, in 1 km tile folders, with a manifest listing sha256, CRS, vertical datum, realisation, source edition and attribution, as Vista's release manifest does. Keep raw LAS, COG windows and intermediate rasters outside the repository; commit only derived files well under 50 MiB (warning) and 100 MiB (block). Serve from GitHub Pages (site at most 1 GB) with lazy per-tile loading; use release assets for optional large packs. Build reproducibly from a Python script that records tool and data versions. Benchmark against Vista on total shipped bytes per building including index files: 1,072 B central and 408 B extension (computed), not the 982 B and 320 B mesh-only figures. Measured source sizes for planning: City tile zip 1.007 GB, LidarBC 2025 tile 239 MB, 2016 tile 62.9 MB, 1 m DEM sheet 236 MB.

modules.name: Accuracy audit versus Vista and published heights
modules.design_question: How far do LiDAR-derived heights and terrain differ from Vista's OSM and SRTM context once Vista's distorted frame is corrected, and do they reproduce published checks?
modules.method: Define a regression set run in EPSG:3157. (a) About 40 downtown towers with published heights. (b) 20 or more UBC buildings with ubcv_Structures bldgheight (2021 LiDAR). (c) 200 random downtown buildings, LiDAR height versus Vista height, after re-projecting Vista geometry with the documented Vista-to-UTM transform (Vista formula, then lon/lat, then UTM). (d) 500 terrain points, Vista SRTM 60 m surface versus City DTM after datum calibration; also the z shifts Vista applied when it re-seated buildings on SRTM. (e) Cone-flip analysis: for each protected view, count buildings whose cone-intersection status changes when OSM heights are replaced by LiDAR heights, using test H_cone values. (f) Existing-tower regression against reconstructed cones (M04). Report median, p95 and maximum absolute error by tier, with maps and histograms. Run the numbers in CI on a small fixture tile (490000_5459000). Publish an accuracy statement beside the data. Vista facts: central model 9,897 buildings (1,441 measured OSM heights, 3,656 from levels, 4,800 estimated); extension 51,510 from current OSM; local frame uses 110,574 m per degree of latitude.

modules.design_question: How are building currency, attribution and licence obligations tracked per layer so the open-source release stays compliant?
modules.method: Maintain layers.json with id, publisher, URL, retrieval date, upstream modified date, licence, required attribution text, CRS, realisation, vertical datum, edition (for example MRDEM 1.2), acquisition date and checksum. Generate in-app credits and README attribution from it. Flag buildings completed after the City LiDAR acquisition (7 and 9 Sept 2022) using LidarBC 2025 differencing and an override table of published heights with citations (for example The Stack 2023, The Butterfly 2024). Keep ODbL layers (OSM, Overture) as a separate database from City layers; do not merge OSM geometry into City-derived products without a licence opinion. City layers: OGL-Vancouver is reported to be OGL-BC 2.0 with the name replaced (attribution only; City text unread); default OGL-BC wording is 'Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - British Columbia.' Use the City's own string once confirmed. Re-pull the view-cones dataset when its portal modified date changes (now 2026-10-19; Vista snapshot 2026-09-21). Include Copernicus credit text for MRDEM and GLO-30. Ask the City whether combined-layer attribution is acceptable.

flags.claim: Google Open Buildings can supply Vancouver footprints.
flags.correction: Coverage is Africa, South and South-East Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean; Canada is not listed and the page names no height field.
flags.detail: Use City LiDAR, City 2015 footprints, OSM, Overture or Microsoft instead.

flags.claim: City building-footprint datasets carry height fields.
flags.correction: Only the 2009 set has elevations and heights, as roof-facet rows under 2009 conditions; 2015 and 1999 sets are geometry only.
flags.detail: 2009 rows near Shangri-La show a tower under construction; do not treat them as current.

flags.claim: The City publishes DEM or DSM products derived from 2018 and 2022 LiDAR.
flags.correction: 2018 and 2022 are zipped LAS tiles only; the only City raster DEM is the 2013 1 m GeoTIFF (1.91 GB).
flags.detail: We must derive DTM and DSM ourselves (M04).

flags.claim: EPSG:26910 is NAD83(CSRS) UTM zone 10N.
flags.correction: 26910 is NAD83 (original); NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N is EPSG:3157. City LiDAR states NAD83(CSRS) 4.0.0.BC.1.GVRD.
flags.detail: EPSG remarks say sub-metre accuracy needs the CSRS code; City orthophotos are labelled EPSG:26910.

flags.claim: All elevation sources can be merged without datum work.
flags.correction: City LiDAR is CGVD28GVRD; HRDEM and MRDEM are CGVD2013; SRTM is EGM96; GLO-30 is EGM2008; OSM heights are relative.
flags.detail: CHS offsets imply about +0.12 m between CGVD2013 and CGVD28 (unverified); MRDEM v1.1 moved heights about 0.4 m.

flags.claim: Vista README: terrain is '60 m SRTM'.
flags.correction: SRTM 1 arc-second (about 30.9 x 20.1 m cells) sampled at 60 m (extension) and 300 m (backdrop), EGM96; supplied-model terrain source and datum are unrecorded.
flags.detail: Actual vertical error is about 10 m (USGS), unusable for cone height limits.

flags.claim: Vista's local equirectangular frame is adequate for cone tests.
flags.correction: It differs from UTM 10N by about 5 m at 2.5 km and up to 34 m at its extent corners (computed).
flags.detail: Fine for visuals; use UTM or a per-view ENU frame for geometry that touches cone edges. See the r1 FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag on its cause.

flags.claim: Cone maximum geodetic heights are in CGVD28(GVRD).
flags.detail: LTSA 465C keeps CGVD28 as legal-survey datum and the Guidelines say 'maximum geodetic height' (s.2 p.3); the datum definition was not read (403 again in r1). Ask views@vancouver.ca.

flags.claim: View 3.2.1 is 123.201 m geodetic (Barclay) and 361 ft at Thurlow.
flags.detail: Both PDFs were unopened (403); search snippets only (3.2.1 points range 123.2 to 143.4 m). 3.2.1 was among views amended in 2024, so edition and datum may differ.

flags.claim: City OGL-Vancouver and OSM ODbL layers can be combined in one release.
flags.detail: r1: OGL-Vancouver is reported as OGL-BC 2.0 (attribution only), but the City text is unread and a 2014 post records a negative City answer on ODbL compatibility; ODbL share-alike remains. Keep layers separate pending a legal opinion.

flags.claim: 2022 LiDAR is current for every downtown tower.
flags.correction: Acquisition was 7 and 9 Sept 2022; The Stack (2023) and The Butterfly (2024) post-date it.
flags.detail: Flag built_after_lidar and use a cited override table; LidarBC 2025 tiles can confirm.

flags.claim: NRCan Automatically Extracted Buildings has usable heights for Vancouver.
flags.detail: Feature catalogue lists Height Maximum/Minimum, but a WMS GetFeatureInfo query downtown returned empty; coverage unconfirmed.

flags.claim: LidarBC datum and licence are known.
flags.detail: r1: 2025 tiles state CGVD2013(2010); 2016 index field is blank; licence is OGL-BC in the portal record but 'Access Only' in the catalogue field. Still conflicting.

flags.claim: SRTM is adequate for 'as accurate as possible' North Shore mountains.
flags.correction: MRDEM-30 (about 1 to 5 m RMSE per earlier spec table) is available over the same area; SRTM is about 10 m.
flags.detail: Slopes amplify horizontal error (20 m CE90 on 30 degrees gives 11.5 m vertical). HRDEM 1 m does not reach the ridges (r1).

flags.claim: City LiDAR class names map to LAS codes 1 to 8.
flags.detail: The portal lists class names as a numbered list; ASPRS codes differ (for example water is 9, noise 7). Read the LAS header or a class histogram first.

flags.claim: HRDEM VILLE_VANCOUVER 2013 shares City LiDAR 2013's datum after conversion.
flags.detail: Source LiDAR is CGVD28; HRDEM claims CGVD2013; the STAC item has no vertical field and dates match the City 2013 survey (2013-02-19). Check by sampling against the City DEM (same-source bridge).

flags.claim: HRDEM BC-Lower_Mainland_2016-1m (bbox to 49.5125 N) gives 1 m terrain and skyline for the North Shore front ranges (M05 R2).
flags.correction: A bbox is an envelope. The extent polygon (351 vertices, 2 parts) excludes Grouse, Seymour, Crown, Cypress, Lions samples; HRDEM mosaic DTM is null at Grouse and Seymour; LidarBC has no point-cloud tile there. Ridge terrain is MRDEM-30, GLO-30-derived.
flags.detail: Measured r1: 25% of a 0.02 degree grid north of 49.38 N lies in any LidarBC tile (2016 5%, 2019 15%, 2025 0%). Sample coordinates approximate. LidarBC lists 1 m DEM sheets over the peaks; contents untested.

flags.claim: City LiDAR 2022 heights use the HTGVRDBC00 hybrid geoid.
flags.correction: Portal metadata names the Metro Vancouver Geoid HTMVBC00 (HTMVBC00_Abbbyn.zip). GeoBC: HTMVBC00 equals HTGVRDBC00 extended east to Abbotsford; LTSA approves HTGVRDBC00 in Metro Vancouver.
flags.detail: Registry records HTMVBC00 and epoch 1997. PROJ grid epoch 2010 differs from this; use HT2_1997 variant as primary and quantify locally.

flags.claim: Vista's frame differs from UTM by about 5 m at 2.5 km; a generic projection effect, fine for visuals.
flags.correction: Cause is a wrong latitude constant (110,574 vs 111,215.2 m/deg, 0.58% short) plus 0.19% short longitude scale. Offsets reach 21 m at the north edge of the supplied model and 34 m at the SE corner; 14 m at 2.5 km north.
flags.detail: The supplied Rhino model fits the formula to 0.08 m, so it carries the distortion. Re-project Vista assets with a documented forward and inverse transform.

flags.claim: OGL-Vancouver may be 'viral' (share-alike), so City layers cannot be combined (M08).
flags.correction: The 2011 commentary predates the current licence. OGL-Vancouver is reported as OGL-BC 2.0 with the name replaced; the OGL-BC 2.0 text read is attribution-only. Share-alike comes from ODbL.
flags.detail: City's own text and attribution string still unread; keep OSM and Overture separate regardless.

flags.claim: 13 City LiDAR 2022 tiles lie within 2 km of downtown.
flags.correction: 20 tiles intersect a 2 km circle around the Vista anchor; 13 intersect a 1.5 km circle. Plain scripted requests get HTTP 403.
flags.detail: Tile list and rule are in M04 and validation cases; one tile measured 1.007 GB.

flags.claim: MRDEM Table 2 accuracy values (1.04/1.69, 2.55/4.17, GLO-30-derived 1.59 and 4.99 m).
flags.detail: Spec text was extracted in r1 but the table cells were not readable; edition 1.2 says accuracy was recalculated. Treat as unverified, and measured Seymour DSM peak is 12.7 m low.

flags.claim: LidarBC 1 m DEM sheets 092g035, 092g036, 092g045 contain ridge data.
flags.detail: The DEM index lists them over the Grouse, Seymour and West Lion samples, but the point-cloud index has no tile there and 17 to 24 of 64 sub-tiles are missing per sheet. Read pixels to settle.

flags.claim: City LiDAR zips cannot be fetched by script.
flags.detail: Default clients get 403; a HEAD with browser User-Agent and portal Referer returned 200 (size only, nothing downloaded). Terms for automated access unknown; plan browser downloads or ask the City.

flags.claim: City orthophotos labelled EPSG:26910 are in original NAD83.
flags.detail: They may be NAD83(CSRS) mislabelled; original NAD83 differs by up to about 1 m in BC. Test on LiDAR roof corners before applying EPSG:9119.

flags.claim: A 14 person-day core fits before 13 Nov 2026.
flags.correction: Full packet is about 39 person-days. Core slice: M01 1.5, M02 2, M03 3, M04 2, M05 2, M06 1.5, M07 1, M08 1.
flags.detail: 17 working days to 13 Nov (excluding 11 Nov) for 2 students at an assumed 40% share is about 13.6; tight.
